name: The microbiome & human health

papers.title: Microbiome recovery after antibiotic exposure
papers.abstract: Longitudinal sampling can characterize the recovery of human gut microbial communities after antibiotic exposure. Can longitudinal microbiome profiles predict recovery after antibiotic exposure?

papers.title: Diet, microbial metabolism, and intestinal inflammation
papers.abstract: Diet and microbial metabolism may contribute to variation in intestinal inflammation. Does dietary variation explain differences in microbial metabolite profiles during intestinal inflammation?

papers.title: Host transcriptional response in inflammatory bowel disease
papers.abstract: Human host gene expression offers a complementary view of inflammatory bowel disease and its clinical course. Do host transcriptomic signatures distinguish treatment responders from non-responders in inflammatory bowel disease?

papers.title: Microbial predictors of clinical remission
papers.abstract: Linking baseline microbiome composition to subsequent outcomes requires longitudinal human data. Are baseline microbial communities associated with subsequent clinical remission?

papers.title: Following disease activity over time
papers.abstract: Repeated measurements of clinical outcomes may help characterize the course of inflammatory bowel disease in human participants. Can repeated clinical measurements distinguish transient inflammation from persistent disease activity?

papers.title: Connecting microbiome and metabolomics measurements
papers.abstract: Multi-omic approaches may connect human gut microbial composition to metabolic readouts and clinical outcomes. Does combining metabolomics with microbiome composition improve prediction of treatment response?

datasets.title: Qiita longitudinal human gut microbiome antibiotic exposure studies

datasets.title: GEO inflammatory bowel disease host transcriptomics cohorts
datasets.description: Host transcriptomic datasets from intestinal tissue and blood in IBD, including disease state, treatment response, and inflammation markers.
